yarn.meaning: All the safety points survive, in order. Additions mostly elaborate ("like a golf buggy or a convertible" for open vehicles). But it reframes the US notice for an Australian reader: "in that country" for "in this country" and "Call 911 (it's the States, remember, not triple-zero)", which shifts who is speaking.
yarn.sense: Most terms fit ("power point", "Mobiles", "bucketin' down", "quick smart", "in strife"). "Some bastards have the sense to get inside" uses a term of abuse for the sensible people, which strains.
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like a real Aussie yarn: "No word of a lie", "have a crack at ya", "Don't muck about", "ya galah". "a lot of folks" leans American.
yarn.register: A full level-5 retelling throughout, with swearing ("bloody", "bastards", "flamin'") within vulgarity 2.
yarn.tone: Stays a serious warning under the yarn ("Not one spot.", "Don't muck about."); "ya galah" adds a jokey jab but does not make it flippant.
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "Some hang about till the storm's right on top of 'em and it starts bucketin' down."
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the NWS lightning notice, with its slogan and its sequence of advice.

engine.meaning: Mostly the original text, but "if thunderstorms are reckoned" loses "expected", and "If some mongrel is struck by lightning" turns the victim into a villain.
engine.sense: Several terms take the wrong sense: "battlers" for people in general, "reckoned" for "expected", "mongrel" for a lightning victim, "Too easy." after CPR instructions.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: stock phrases bolted onto sentence starts ("Crikey,", "Stone the flamin' crows,", "Fair dinkum,", "So anyway,"); US "Cell phones" and "electrical outlet" left in.
engine.register: Heavy-handed swearing reaches level 5 by brute force, but the underlying text is largely untranslated ("Substantial buildings and hard-topped vehicles are safe options."). "Fair fuckin' dinkum" is within vulgarity 2.
engine.tone: "Oh, shit," and "Too easy." make a life-safety notice flippant; calling the victim "some mongrel" is callous.
engine.flow: Jarring joins: "Anyway, Understandin' the Threat" as a heading, "Well, Cell phones", "Well, lightning Victims", "punters’s behaviour".
engine.essence: Recognisable as the lightning notice, but its sober authority is lost.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives, in order, with no reframing: "If everyone stuck to those simple rules, the number of people killed and hurt by lightning in this country could drop a hell of a lot."
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit their context: "on the cards", "power point", "Mobiles", "bucketing down", "piss-poor planning", "quick smart".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural throughout: "Rain shelters, little sheds and open vehicles are bloody useless", "Some hang about till the storm's right overhead".
unharnessed.register: Clearly Aussie and lively, with swearing inside vulgarity 2 ("piss-poor", "bloody"), but more a casual retelling than a full level-5 pub yarn.
unharnessed.tone: Stays a serious, practical warning throughout.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Whether someone cops a lightning strike comes down to how they carry on when there's storms about."
unharnessed.variety: Varied, though "when there's storms about" and "how they carry on" recur.

yarn.quote: Some bastards have the sense to get inside at the first sign of a storm
yarn.original: While some people move inside at the first signs of a thunderstorm
yarn.why: A term of abuse applied to the people doing the right thing; strains the sense.

yarn.quote: the number of people hurt or killed by lightning in that country
yarn.original: the number of lightning casualties in this country
yarn.why: Changes the speaker from the US agency to an outsider.

yarn.quote: Call 911 (it's the States, remember, not triple-zero)
yarn.why: Aside reframes the notice for Australian readers; colour, but it shifts the voice.

yarn.quote: a lot of folks leave it way too long
yarn.original: many people wait far too long

engine.quote: Oh, shit, there's no safe place outside
engine.original: There is no safe place outside
engine.why: Swear bolted onto a safety notice; makes it flippant.

engine.quote: Fair fuckin' dinkum, also, keep away from outside doors
engine.original: Also, keep away from outside doors
engine.why: Stock phrase bolted on with a jarring join.

engine.quote: many battlers wait far too fuckin' long
engine.original: many people wait far too long
engine.why: "battlers" means people doing it tough, not people in general; repeated throughout.

engine.quote: If some mongrel is struck by lightning
engine.original: If someone is struck by lightning
engine.why: Insults the victim; changes the sense of the first-aid section.
Flippant added close after CPR instructions.

engine.quote: Well, Cell phones and cordless phones are safe.
engine.original: Cell phones and cordless phones are safe.
engine.why: US "Cell phones" left in, with a filler bolted on.

unharnessed.quote: Some people head inside at the first sign of a storm
unharnessed.original: While some people move inside at the first signs of a thunderstorm
unharnessed.why: Many lines stay fairly plain; a little light for level 5.

unharnessed.original: when thunderstorms are in the area

summaries.yarn: A vivid, natural level-5 yarn that keeps every safety point; a few reframings and an odd "bastards".
summaries.engine: Mostly untranslated, with swears and stock phrases bolted on and several wrong-sense terms; the safety tone is undercut.
summaries.unharnessed: Faithful, natural and serious, a notch lighter than level 5.
